source.image: the file is the loaded image behind a 0x100-byte header: main+X = file offset 0x100+X (checked: AArch64 code decodes sanely at main+0x96E2C8)
source.parser: throwaway python3 + capstone AArch64 (outside system/gbox); every address below was decoded from the bytes

instructions: 0x96E2CC ldr w8,[x22] (x22=slot+8 weapon word); and #0xff00 ==0x100 -> player weapon; w8<0x150
0x96E2E8 ldrb w9,[x20,#0x25] upgrade level of the slot
0x96E324-0x96E32C s1 = *(float*)([x25]+0x93C)  shot-motion frame (x25 holds sPlayer::mpInstance, main+0x1CF1C98)
0x96E330 fcmp frame,(firing_speed+offset); b.lt skip; else 0x96E338 strb 1,[player+0x37B0] (trigger re-arm)
fire_action_rearm.rule: re-arm trigger when shot-motion frame >= firing_speed[level] + interval_offset; no fps constant is involved

action_timer.reading: [x19+0x48] -= *(float*)(*(main+0x1CF08A0)+0x34) * player+0x1A08 ; the frame delta times the player's time scale. Another timer of the same action; what sets +0x48 not determined

fire_timer_60_to_4800.switch: no fps constant in the fire action; the pace is frame delta (global main+0x1CF08A0 -> +0x34) x player time scale (+0x1A08), which is what the mod writes

why_5x.measured_in_repo: re5_switch_mods.py line 80 FIRE_MAX=5.0 and fire_rate() line 223 k=min(k,FIRE_MAX): the 5x is the operator's loadout cap in the mod (2026-10-28), not a game limit. SNIPER_FIRE_X=30 already exceeds it.
why_5x.game_side: live docs: x2 4.7, x4 8.7, x8 15.3, x32 16.7, x80 24.7 shots/s. The re-arm check runs once per fire-action update and sets one trigger byte, so at most one shot per update; the ceiling is inferred (not verified) to be the update rate (Citron 40-60 fps; a shot also needs the motion to restart at frame 0)
